solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rosa fled from town in Lincolnshire

indicators.note: letters made from other letters are rearranged, so 'from' here signals a reshuffle of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A woman called Rosa has run away from some Lincolnshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fled' looks like the verb of the sentence but is fodder: ROSA and FLED together, rearranged as signalled by 'from', make the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleaford is a market town in the county of Lincolnshire in eastern England.

clue.text: Oriental article authentic and heavenly

parts.note: E for East, the Orient
the definite article
authentic means real

explanation.surface: An Eastern piece of writing is genuine and divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal describes something airy and otherworldly, as delicate as if from the heavens.

clue.text: Polish workers on increase

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece written on another comes after it, below it

parts.note: worker bees, the crossword's standard workers
to wax is to grow, as the moon does

explanation.surface: A Polish workforce is getting bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised to look like the nationality; it is the verb or noun for shining.
explanation.definitionFit: Beeswax is used as a furniture polish, so the word names that polish.

clue.text: Lady, not one on piano, started exercises

indicators.note: 'not one' tells us to leave the letter for one out of the piano word

parts.note: JOANNA is Cockney rhyming slang for piano (pronounced 'pianna')
A means one, as in a single

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is where it started, so take the first letter of exercises

explanation.surface: A woman, not one for the piano, began her exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang, a London habit, rhymes JOANNA with 'pianna'.
explanation.definitionFit: Joanne is a woman's name, so any lady could be called it.

clue.text: Set of parts, nearly a dozen found in litter

parts.note: a kit is a set of parts for assembling something
ten falls just short of twelve

explanation.surface: A self-assembly kit with almost twelve pieces has turned up among the rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' suggests rubbish; here it is a brood of young animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A young cat is born as one of a litter, so it is literally found in one.

clue.text: Ring for order?

parts.note: ringing for order reads like a bell for silence, but means phoning those who keep law and order

explanation.surface: Someone rings a bell to bring a noisy room to order.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialling the emergency number for the police is ringing for law and order to be restored.

clue.text: Reverse charge

parts.note: reads as a collect phone call, but means a charge made going back the other way

explanation.surface: A telephone call paid for by the person receiving it.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse-charge call is one billed to the person called.
explanation.definitionFit: A military charge made in return against an attacking enemy is a charge in reverse.

clue.text: Strangest idea developed in West Sussex

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An odd notion evolved in a southern English county.
explanation.definitionFit: East Grinstead is a town located in the county of West Sussex in southern England.

clue.text: Benevolent chap taken in by Hugh, say

indicators.note: one piece taken in by another sits inside it
'say' signals how the name sounds when spoken

parts.note: the name Hugh is pronounced like the word for a colour
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A kindly fellow is welcomed by someone named Hugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means compassionate and kind, the same as benevolent.

clue.text: End of disease in hospital initially exceptionally clean

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a hospital
-ITIS is the ending on many disease names, like tonsillitis

indicators.note: the word's first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Once a disease ends, a hospital becomes spotless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of disease' looks like an instruction to take the last letter E; it is the suffix ITIS. 'in' joins the pieces, which stand in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanitise is to make something hygienic, the verb sense of clean.

clue.text: Not all of the crawfish had been left uncooked

indicators.note: only part of the word crawfish is used, so the answer lies within it

explanation.surface: Some of the crayfish was still not cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw food is food that has not been cooked.

clue.text: Fit oarsman?

definitions.meaning: a sudden seizure, such as an apoplectic attack
the rower nearest the stern who sets the pace

explanation.definitionFit: A stroke is both a medical seizure and the rower setting the crew's rhythm.

clue.text: One in the fiery furnace sleeping before making quarter turn

indicators.note: the sleeping piece comes before the rest

parts.note: abed means in bed, sleeping
NE, north-east, is a quarter of the compass
a turn is a go, as in a game

explanation.surface: Someone sleeping until they must take a quarter turn.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego survived being thrown into a fiery furnace.
explanation.definitionFit: Abednego was one of three Biblical men cast into the furnace and unharmed.

clue.text: Second name included for deoxyribonucleic acid

indicators.note: the answer is included within the words second name

explanation.surface: A second name added to a form about genetic material.
explanation.definitionFit: The usual abbreviation for deoxyribonucleic acid, the genetic molecule.

clue.text: Led off behind grating to find hotplate

indicators.note: the rearranged piece comes behind the first

parts.note: a grid is a grating

indicators.note: something gone off is spoiled or out of order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone was taken away behind bars to locate a cooking surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A griddle is a flat heated plate for cooking.

clue.text: Fingerprint expert

explanation.definitionFit: Dab is British slang for a fingerprint, and a dab hand is an expert.

clue.text: Commander embraced girl model

parts.note: CIC is Commander-in-Chief
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: An officer hugged a young woman who poses for photos.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is a standard example or exemplar, a model of its kind.

clue.text: Standard-bearer is light supporter

parts.note: a standard is a lamp standard, so the bearer of it holds up a street light

explanation.surface: A flag carrier is a minor fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A street post holds up a lamp: a standard in the lighting sense.

clue.text: Provided only that one's farewell came first

indicators.note: the goodbye piece comes before the other

parts.note: so long means goodbye
A'S, the letter for one with its 's

explanation.surface: Someone said goodbye first.
explanation.definitionFit: So long as means on condition that, the same as provided only that.

clue.text: At home ineffective fellow included to provoke powerful response

parts.note: in means at home
a lame excuse is an ineffective one

explanation.surface: An ineffective man at home stirs up a strong reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflame is to provoke passion or anger, stirring a strong reaction.

clue.text: Bob turns terribly inflexible

indicators.note: done terribly, in a muddle, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bob becomes awfully unyielding.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn means obstinate and unbending, refusing to be flexible.

clue.text: Explosive sausage?

parts.note: a sausage that might blow up, playing on two meanings of one word: a firework and a sausage

explanation.surface: A sausage that bursts in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a banger is both an everyday word for a sausage and a small firework.
explanation.definitionFit: Banger is British slang for a sausage and also for a firework that explodes.

clue.text: Level with writing about a couple I left

parts.note: writing about a subject is writing on it

indicators.note: I left means the letter I leaves

parts.note: a couple is a pair
the letter I

explanation.surface: Equal to a text concerning two people, one of whom has departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at the same standard as something means being level with it.

clue.text: Pester doctor in case

parts.note: MO is medical officer
lest means in case

explanation.surface: Bother a physician in a legal matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To molest is to harass or bother, an older sense of pester.

clue.text: Fine work affected dandy

parts.note: F for fine, as on pencils
OP is opus, a work

explanation.surface: Excellent work has influenced a dapper man.
explanation.definitionFit: A fop is a vain man fussy about dress, a dandy with affectations.

clue.text: Animals I removed from canvas sheet

indicators.note: re-moved, moved again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Animals taken away from a tent sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainsail is a ship's principal sail, a sheet of canvas.

clue.text: Gratify said animal

indicators.note: the animal word is said aloud

parts.note: a panda is an animal

explanation.surface: Please the beast mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: In British non-rhotic speech PANDA and PANDER sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To pander is to indulge or gratify someone's wishes.

clue.text: Eager one's hot and very enthusiastic

parts.note: keen means eager
A'S, the letter for one with its 's
mustard is hot

explanation.surface: Someone eager is fiery and full of zeal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone extremely eager and enthusiastic.
